text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a specific endpoint. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access protected resources, you usually need authentication, often through an API key or token. Be careful with rate limits, because sending too many requests can block your access. Finally, always include error handling in your code. Servers can fail or return unexpected responses, so check status codes and handle problems gracefully.
